name: Robin / Helios
notes: Intro with Robin Hayes, who booked from a Gmail address. She is VP of Sales at Iris Health. Team of about 40 AEs. She needs a forecasting cadence; they are coming off spreadsheets and a light CRM.

action_items.text: Send Robin a first-call recap and a proposed sandbox for an Iris Health AE pod
Share AE count by pod and the current forecast spreadsheet

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Robin, thanks for the time. The invite came through as Gmail — I don't want to assume a company. Who am I talking to?

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: I'm Robin Hayes. I use Gmail because our IT still hasn't given me a stable alias. I'm at Iris Health — we're a behavioral-health group, not a hospital system. I run sales. About forty AEs across four pods. That's the company, even if the calendar doesn't show it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Iris Health, forty AEs. What made you take a Helios meeting?

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: I need forecasting that the pods will actually live in. Right now each manager has a sheet, I roll them up on Sunday, and the board asks why the number moved. We grew fast. The CRM is a thin Salesforce we barely use. Forecasting is the hole.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Forty AEs is a real rollout, not a founder sheet. Are the pods all selling the same motion?

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: Mostly employer contracts, some clinic partnerships. Cycles are long. I don't need a brand-new CRM. I need a forecast meeting I can inspect. If Helios can't sit on Salesforce, this is a short call.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: We sit on Salesforce. Typical path is one pod as a sandbox, then the other three. For Iris Health I'd want a manager in the first working session so it isn't just you and me nodding at a demo.

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: I can bring Devon, who runs the East pod. I should also say: please use my work context, not this Gmail, once we're past intro. The Gmail is how I booked because I was on a plane. Mail about Iris should go to me at work once I have the alias, and I'll send that.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Send the alias when you have it. Until then I'll recap here. Any other tools in the mix — Gong, a CPQ, a data team?

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: Gong for calls, no CPQ, no dedicated RevOps yet. That's why I need something an ops-minded VP can run. We're our own shop — Iris Health, forty AEs, behavioral health. Forecasting is the job.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: I'll send a recap and a sandbox proposal for Iris Health. If you can share headcount by pod and a sanitized forecast sheet, I can make the first session look like your Monday, not a generic health demo.

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: I'll send the sheet. Timing: I'd like a working session before September. Board is mid-September and I don't want another quarter of Sunday roll-ups.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: We can do that. I'll propose two times. Thanks Robin — good to meet you, and thanks for spelling out Iris Health. The Gmail invite was a little mysterious.

transcript.speaker: Robin Hayes
transcript.text: Yeah. Robin Hayes, Iris Health, forty AEs, we need forecasting. Talk soon.
